name: html-nav-collapsed-css-toggle
description: A header holds an in-flow destination list (a signaled container, not a <nav> landmark) beside a labelless <label> whose only child is the empty span CSS paints as a 3-bar glyph. A CSS-hidden duplicate of the same destinations names the collapsed surface. Below the breakpoint the source hides the in-flow list and shows the toggle; the JS that opened the duplicate is not carried. The in-flow menu must emit overlayMenu 'mobile' with Core's native open control, the toggle must not surface as a dead button, and the collapsed duplicate must not emit a second navigation. Before this fix, equivalent-variant detection only compared <nav> landmarks and the single-span glyph was not a hamburger, so overlayMenu stayed 'never' and phone visitors lost every destination.

source_reference.notes: Product-neutral fixture reduced from a captured header that collapses its in-flow list behind a CSS-drawn toggle below a max-width breakpoint and keeps an equivalent overlay copy. Detection is structural (link signature, collapsed-surface identity, single empty glyph host); no vendor-specific markup is referenced.

legacy_comparison.reason: This upstream primitive fixture has no downstream legacy comparison.
